 Judgment
(Delivered on 14.07.2023)

1. By way of present revision petition, petitioner impugns the order dated 28.09.2022, passed by ld.
CMM, North-West, Rohini Courts in Case No. 2208/2020, titled as Richa Aggarwal Vs Vinay aggarwal whereby ld. CMM has dismissed the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
2.
Grounds taken by petitioner are that ld. MM has passed the C.R. No. 412/2022 Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState.

entities.text: C.R. No. 412/2022 Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page no. 2 impugned order without considering the allegations which requires to be investigated as the same cannot be proved by complainant by oral testimony.

It is further submitted that role of bank officials have to be ascertained as alleged persons have got issued new cheque book in the name of petitioner at their address, when she was living separately from alleged persons,
which petitioner came to know through RTI application.
It is further submitted that alleged persons forged the valuable security of petitioner.

Therefore, as the complaint of complainant/petitioner disclosed commission of cognizable offence and it requires to be investigated by investigating agency, order of ld. MM is against the principles of natural justice.
3. Brief facts of the case are that petitioner/complainant got married with alleged Vinay Aggarwal on 11.12.2009 and since March 2016 she is living separately from her husband Vinay Aggarwal.
Complainant/petitioner has an bank account with Canara Bank, respondent no. 6 herein.
After her separation, alleged persons had withdrawn money from her account on different occasions, without her consent, by forging her signatures on her cheques.

4. Ld. Trial Court dismissed the application holding that, "After carefully scrutinizing the entire complainant as well as the documents on record it is limpid that the entire issue appears to be outcome of matrimonial disputes already pending between the complainant and the alleged.

Further, the alleged transaction C.R. No. 412/2022 Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState. Page no. 3 have taken place during the period of 13.01.2017 to 29.12.2017 but the complainant has not made a complaint before the bank or to the police regarding the said transactions.

entities.text: Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState. Page no. 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The complainant made the present complaint on 22.07.2019 around one and half year later of the alleged transactions.
It is a admitted fact that matrimonial litigation is going between the parties.

The status report further Richa Agarwal vs The State on 14 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160695890/
2 mentions that the complainant has also filed a similar complaint in PS Subji Mandi and Tis Hazari Courts, against the allged.

entities.text: Richa Agarwal vs The State on 14 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no material on record to suggest the commission of any cognizable offence at this stage, and moreover the entire issue appears to be of civil in nature which has just been given criminal overtone.

Hence, in my considered opinion, no custodial interrogation of the proposed accused is required and no cognizable offence appears to be made out in the present case, hence, to my mind, there appears not ground to issue directions to SHO PS Subhash Place to register an FIR as there is nothing, for which the police assistance is called for.
Accordingly, the application U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. stands disposed off."
5. Submissions heard.
Record perused.
6. Ld. MM appears to have committed a mistake by holding that it is a matrimonial dispute between husband and wife.

The allegations against the alleged persons were that they have fraudulently got issued cheque book in the name of petitioner at their address while the petitioner was living separately and after C.R. No. 412/2022 Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState.

entities.text: C.R. No. 412/2022 Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page no. 4 forging her signatures, money was withdrawn from her account.
It is also submitted by ld.
Counsel for petitioner that this could have been done with the connivance of bank officials as the petitioner was not supplied with her bank statement and she had to apply an RTI to get the same.
Documents received in RTI show that while petitioner was living separately from alleged persons, new cheque book was issued in her name at the address of alleged persons.
The record also shows that while opening the bank account the phone number given in the bank was of the husband of the petitioner against whom she has alleged forgery of valuable security.
Therefore, petitioner did not get any notification regarding withdrawal of money from the bank.

7. It is submitted by ld. Counsel for respondent that since all the documents are in possession of petitioner now there is nothing remaining to be investigated by police as no custodial interrogation is required and nothing is required to be discovered or recovered.

It is also submitted that thee is a huge delay in filing the complaint and because of this delay, as mentioned in the status report of IO,
no evidence would be available.
8.
It is true that most of the evidence in this case is documentary and some of that is already in possession of petitioner.
However, the allegations are of forgery of valuable security and by committing that forgery petitioner has been deprived of her money to the tune almost 18 lacs.
The correctness of allegations can only be ascertained by investigation and C.R. No. 412/2022 Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState.

entities.text: C.R. No. 412/2022 Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page no. 5 investigation is required in this case because forgery cannot be proved by oral examination but after scientific examination of documents.
9. The allegations shows that there may be some bank officials involved whose names are to be unearthed.
Therefore, it is a fit case where not only the cognizable offence was disclosed but investigation was required.

Yet ld. MM, considering that it is a dispute between husband and wife,
did not order the investigation and considered it to be a civil dispute.
10. It is not the case that the allegations were made after much delay as the petitioner had already filed a complaint before CWC on which an FIR no. 367/20 was registered and investigated.

This Richa Agarwal vs The State on 14 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160695890/
3 complaint also contains the allegation of the forgery of the cheques of petitioner and misuse of same.

entities.text:

3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Today ld. Counsel for respondent submitted that the charge sheet in FIR no. 367/2020 has been filed and accused persons have received the copy and
on request ld. Counsel has graciously allowed this Court to peruse the copy of that charge sheet.

11. The investigation in charge sheet of FIR no. 367/20 is restricted only to offences under Section 498A & 406 IPC and qua the allegation of forgery into the cheques and misuse no investigation is conducted as the application under Section 156(3) Cr.p.C. was pending.
This application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. is the same application in which the ld. MM C.R. No. 412/2022 Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState.

entities.text: MM C.R. No. 412/2022 Richa Aggarwal Vs. TheState
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page no
. 6 passed impugned order.

Therefore, a serious crime of forgery of valuable security and its misuse to deprive the petitioner of her money, which in her account will always remain her istridhan from whatever source that money have come.

12. As mandated by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Lalita Kumari Vs. State of UP & Ors. (2012) 4 SCC 1 the SHO PS concerned is duty bound to register the FIR on receipt of an information regarding cognizable offence and since this case requires the scientific investigation of the documents to bring on record the forgery and nexus between the bank officials and the persons who committed forgery,
which the complaint will not be able to bring on record by herself, the impugned order is set aside.

entities.text: Lalita Kumari Vs. State of UP & Ors. (2012) 4 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. SHO PS Subhash Place is directed to investigate the complaint of petitioner after formally registering an FIR.

It is, however, reminded that power to investigate is different from power to arrest and liberty being the most valuable right enshrined in Constitution of India should not be disturbed unless there are grave reasons for the same.

Therefore, the IO shall keep in mind the mandate of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar as well as Satender Kumar Antil Vs. SBI before proceeding to take any step effecting the liberty of any one during investigation of this case.
